categories.category_definition: Playing a quiet, non-forcing "natural-looking" move — a pawn push, routine piece development, rook re-filing, or king repositioning — at a moment when the position demanded an immediate forcing response (capture, check, defense, or winning tactic), squandering the critical tempo.

subclusters.name: Premature push or development over forced tactic
Flank pawn push burns forcing tempo
Piece abandons critical file or duty
Rim pawn push over decisive shot
Wing pawn push exposes uncastled king
Rook drifts to passive rim file

misfits.reason: Describes the king actively capturing an advanced g/h-pawn and inviting a decisive attack — a greedy material grab that exposes the king, not a slow/non-forcing tempo-waster. Belongs in 'Greedy Captures' or 'King Walks Into Danger'.

The king (or pawn) advances onto a tactically vulnerable, forkable square — the move loses because the destination is hit, i.e. walking into a tactic, not because a quiet move squandered tempo. Belongs in 'King Walks Into Danger' / overextension.

categories.category_definition: Choosing an intuitively appealing move — quiet development, a pawn push, a repositioning, a tempting capture, or an aggressive-looking sortie — while ignoring the position's concrete forcing demand (an available capture, check, defense, or mate).

misfits.reason: This is an endgame conversion/technique error — misplacing a major piece on the wrong rank (missing a cut-off) in already-winning endgames — not a failure to spot the position's concrete forcing demand. Belongs in an endgame-technique / sloppy-conversion category.

categories.category_definition: The player makes a plausible-looking move — repositioning a piece to an "active" square, giving a check, pushing a pawn, or relocating the king — that follows general logic but fails to meet the position's urgent, concrete demand (defending a piece, the forcing win, or king safety).

subclusters.name: Drifting To Edge Or Back Rank
Rook Abandons Back Rank, Mate Follows

misfits.reason: All 10 positions are the king capturing an adjacent enemy queen and transitioning into a LOST pure pawn endgame. The mistake is a miscalculated exchange / endgame-evaluation error (automatic, greedy recapture into a losing K+P endgame), not a failure to meet an urgent tactical or king-safety demand. Belongs with greedy/miscalculated captures.

categories.category_definition: Playing a slow, non-forcing move — a pawn push, piece repositioning, development, or king move — at a sharp moment that demanded an immediate concrete or forcing response, surrendering the win or the game.

subclusters.name: Slow Pawn Push Over Forcing Move
King Move Or Castle Over Tactics
Quiet Pawn Push Over Decisive Strike

misfits.reason: Describes an over-aggressive forcing move (a tempting capture/check/advance) that walks into a refutation — the player IS being forcing, just calculating wrongly. This is a greedy/premature-capture error, the opposite of the slow, non-forcing passivity that defines this category.

categories.category_definition: Committal pawn pushes, piece sorties, sacrifices, and trades that look purposeful but loosen the player's own king, abandon a defender or shield, or overextend a piece into immediate capture, handing the opponent a punishing reply.

misfits.reason: A queen wing-check (Qa4/Qh5 etc.) against a centralized king that is trivially blocked by a developing move. The mistake is a pointless, tempo-losing check, not a self-weakening of king safety or material exposure. Belongs in a 'Pointless Checks / Tempo Loss' category, not here.

categories.category_definition: The player answers an urgent position with a slow, non-forcing repositioning move — usually sending a piece to the rim, edge, corner, or back rank — instead of the concrete forcing action (capture, defense, or threat) the moment demanded.

subclusters.name: King And Queen Drift To Edge

misfits.reason: Greedy capture, not passive drift: a rook grabs a rim pawn and the material grab walks into checkmate. This is a 'Greedy Captures / material over mate' mistake — an active capturing error, not a slow repositioning to the edge.

Greedy capture missing a tactic: a knight grabs a passive rim piece while overlooking a stronger fork. Same 'Greedy Captures' family as 940 — chasing material instead of the winning tactic, distinct from the passive/rim-drift theme of this category.

categories.category_definition: Relocating a piece or pawn to a more natural-, active-, or central-looking square when it was already performing an essential function on its current one — defending, blocking a line, restraining an enemy piece, holding a dominant outpost, or guarding the king — or when the position demanded a concrete move instead.

subclusters.name: Vacating A Restraint Or Blocking Square

categories.category_definition: Playing a natural, principled, or prophylactic move — a slow pawn push, routine development, castling, fianchetto, or a king tuck/activation — when the position concretely demanded a specific forcing move (a capture, check, tactic, or precise king maneuver), and getting punished for it.

subclusters.name: Wing pawn push squanders endgame tempo
Prophylactic rim pawn push over action
Prophylactic king tuck over forcing move
Pawn push blocks own piece or king shelter
Passed pawn push over piece move
Mistimed king safety, king in center
Slow pawn push or queen drift

misfits.reason: Bxf7+ on move 3 — an unsound minor-piece sacrifice for a single pawn. This is premature over-aggression (a flashy forcing move that fails), the opposite of the slow/principled autopilot play this category captures.
Greek Gift bishop sacrifice (Bxh7+/Bxh2+) that is tactically unsound. An unjustified sacrifice is over-aggression, not the passive/routine move this category is about.
Sacrificing a full minor piece on the castled king's shelter (h3/h6/g6) for one pawn hoping for a mating attack. Unsound sacrifice / over-aggression, a different mistake type than slow play.
Pawn check that drives the enemy king to safety — a pointless/harmful forcing check. Belongs to the distinct 'Pointless Checks' mistake, not autopilot/passive play.
Diagonal pawn check that drives the wandering enemy king to safety. A counterproductive forcing check (Pointless Checks), opposite of the slow non-forcing move this category captures.
Premature bishop check/attack along a long diagonal that is easily blocked or parried. An over-aggressive forcing move that backfires, not the principled/slow play of this category.

categories.category_definition: Playing a generically appealing move — natural development, active repositioning, a tempting check, a flank attack, or a material grab — on instinct, while overlooking the specific concrete move the position required (a forcing tactic or a defensive necessity).

subclusters.name: Moving A Piece Off Its Duty

categories.category_definition: The player makes a natural-looking, plan-driven move — a passive retreat, a rook maneuver, or a reflex pawn push/promotion — at a moment that concretely demanded a forcing, defensive, or precise response instead.

subclusters.name: Passive Retreat to Own Back Rank

misfits.reason: This is a quiet developing move (rook to an open file) that simply leaves the rook en prise to the enemy queen, with back-rank mate preventing recapture. The primary error is hanging a piece outright, not playing a routine move at a critical moment. Belongs in a 'Hanging Pieces' category, where the coaching fix (check what the opponent's pieces attack before moving) differs from this category's fix (recognize sharp moments and calculate forcing lines).

categories.category_definition: In sharp, simplified endgames the player makes an imprecise or wrong-priority move — a wasted tempo, a bad king route, a premature flank push, a released pawn tension, or a greedy capture — instead of the single precise move the position demanded to win, draw, or save the game.

subclusters.name: Rim Pawn Pushes And Edge Retreats
Releasing Pawn Tension Gifts A Passer
King To Wrong Square Loses Race

categories.category_definition: Committing a move — a piece relocation, capture, pawn push, or king move — that lands material or the king on a square the opponent immediately punishes, dropping a piece or walking into a decisive tactic because the reply wasn't calculated.

subclusters.name: King Steps Into Forks And Checks

misfits.reason: Passive textbook knight development that misses an available winning tactic — an autopilot/missed-win mistake. Nothing is placed in danger and no material is dropped, so it belongs to a 'Slow/Autopilot Play Misses Tactic' category, not 'Moving Into Danger'.

Initiating a rook trade that surrenders control of an open file — a purely positional concession with no material lost. Unlike the rest of this category (which drops a piece or king safety to an immediate reply), this is a strategic exchange error and belongs in a 'Bad Trades/Concessions' category.

categories.category_definition: The player moves a piece, pawn, or king to chase activity, material, or safety while deserting a defensive duty or leaving a friendly asset undefended and immediately capturable.

subclusters.name: Activating a Piece While Ignoring the Threat

misfits.reason: Pawn pushed at an enemy knight, punished by the knight jumping forward to fork. This is a premature/careless pawn-poke tactic, not deserting a defender.
Pawn advance refuted by a knight capture/fork. Same pawn-push-invites-fork pattern, a distinct mistake from defensive neglect.
Pawn advance vacates the exact square an enemy knight needs to fork. Belongs with the pawn-push-punished-by-knight-fork group, not defensive abandonment.
Capture that dissolves a cramping, space-gaining formation. A positional/strategic concession (releasing tension), not a tactical material drop or an abandoned defender.
Rook move that self-blocks the king's only flight square under mating threat. Self-obstruction / king-trapping is the opposite mechanism from abandoning a defensive duty.

categories.category_definition: The player squanders a critical tempo on a quiet, non-forcing, or merely "improving" move (repositioning, pawn push, king walk, routine recapture, or an obvious-but-imprecise check) when the position demanded one specific forcing or concrete action.
Playing a slow, quiet, non-forcing move — a pawn push, a piece shuffle, or a king step — when the position demanded an immediate forcing move such as a check, capture, or tactical strike.

subclusters.name: Slow Pawn Pushes Over Forcing Moves
Quiet Pushes And Shuffles Over Tactics

misfits.reason: The demanded best move here is a king retreat/sidestep to safety in 7/9 positions — this is a king-safety/defense mistake (failing to move the king out of danger), not a missed forcing win like the rest of the category.

categories.category_definition: Playing a natural-looking move — an active square, a developing move, a pawn push, or a king shuffle — while overlooking the precise or urgent move the position actually required.

subclusters.name: Pawn Push Over Needed Piece Move

misfits.reason: This is a greedy-capture pattern that hangs the player's OWN piece (queen) while grabbing material — a Hanging Pieces / Greedy Captures mistake. The rest of this category is about overlooking the position's required move by playing a quiet or wrong-square move, not about material greed leaving your own piece en prise.

categories.category_definition: At sharp positions where only one or two moves hold, playing a natural-looking, principled, or materially attractive move instead of calculating the single concrete forcing or defensive action the position demands.

subclusters.name: Slow Push or Greedy Grab Over Tactic
Voluntary King Walk and Slow Reroutes
Aggressive Check or Castle Over Defense
Slow King or Knight Move Over Urgency

categories.category_definition: Making a move — a capture, an advance, or a piece relocation — that lands a piece or the king on a square where the opponent has an instant forcing reply (recapture, capture, or check), losing material or king safety on the very next move.

subclusters.name: King and Pieces Step Into Check

categories.category_definition: Playing a superficially reasonable move — an active repositioning, a material grab, or a quiet pawn push — when the position urgently demanded a specific, concrete, forcing response instead.

subclusters.name: Slow Pawn Push, King In Danger
Passive Move When Forcing Play Needed
Routine Improving Move At Critical Moment
